title: Model ingest requirements: version-lock policy, compatibility enrichment, and rollback hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Clarify PRD-level requirements for admitting new open-source model weights into the Redwood catalog with specific guidance on version-lock semantics, required compatibility metadata, runtime probe hooks, and a minimal rollback surface. This ticket consolidates outstanding ambiguities from recent intake cycles: (1) when to require a hard version lock vs. a monitored alias, (2) which compatibility signals (ops/arch/kvcache/quantization) are mandatory, and (3) how the automated rollback/fallback triggers should be surfaced to console and the control plane. Goal: produce a concise acceptance checklist and a short design appendix that engineering and intake reviewers can use to determine whether a model can go to 'catalog-beta' or must stay in 'ephemeral' status.
scope_changes: Add new mandatory compatibility fields: runtime_architecture, recommended_quant_profile, expected_kv_cache_behavior
Introduce a version_lock enum with values: hard, soft, monitored (replaces informal 'pin' terminology used previously)
Require runtime probes artifact (small inference harness) for unpinned/monitored variants before promotion to beta
Add explicit rollback webhook contract to the intake API (lightweight signal for automatic client fallback during regressions)
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Intake schema updated and published: compatibility fields and version_lock enum are defined in the ingestion contract and used by the intake UI and CLI

AC-2: For 'hard' version_lock variants, documentation explains maintenance expectations and upgrade flow; ingress UI enforces hard-lock selection only when upstream guarantees semantic versioning is provided
AC-3: For 'monitored' variants, a runtime probe harness (<=200MB bundle) must be attached; automated sanity tests run in staging and results are visible in the catalog entry

AC-4: Compatibility checklist captures minimum passing conditions for: attention kernel compatibility, kv-cache semantics, max sequence length behavior, and quantization recommendation (int8/int4/float16)
AC-5: Rollback hooks: intake API supports a webhook URL and a TTL for automated fallback events; a minimal spec and example payload are documented in Confluence
AC-6: Console surfaces clear flags for version_lock, last-runtime-probe-run, probe-status, and rollback-hook-config on model detail pages

AC-7: E2E test: submit a monitored variant with failing probe; platform automatically places variant into 'quarantine' state and triggers a rollback webhook; Console shows events and the variant is not routable for production traffic
AC-8: PM + Eng doc approved: PRD addendum (this ticket) reviewed by Runtime, Catalog, and Console leads and linked in the intake workflow
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: prefer 'monitored' semantics over immediate hard-lock to reduce churn for experimental community weights. Runtime team requested explicit kv-cache declaration to avoid hidden failure modes. Console team requested small, visible probe artifacts to make health signals auditable by customers.
follow_up_tasks: Create schema migration ticket in ENG backlog
Design intake UI microcopy for version_lock definition
Author sample probe harness for Llama-3-style kv semantics
